worked_solution:
Suppose the functions ${y}_{1}(x)$ and ${y}_{2}(x)$ are defined on some interval $I.$
The Wronskian $W({y}_{1},{y}_{2})$ of these functions is defined as

$$
W({y}_{1},{y}_{2})=|\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} & {y}_{2} \\ {y}_{1}^{′} & {y}_{2}^{′}\end{aligned}|={y}_{1}{y}_{2}^{′}-{y}_{2}{y}_{1}^{′}.
$$

Recall the following:

- If $W\ne 0$ for at least one $x\in I,$ then ${y}_{1}$ and ${y}_{2}$ are linearly independent.

- If $W=0$ and it’s known that ${y}_{1}$ and ${y}_{2}$ are solutions to the same second-order linear differential equation, then ${y}_{1}$ and ${y}_{2}$ are linearly dependent.

In our case, the Wronskian is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}W({y}_{1},{y}_{2}) & =|\begin{aligned}{x}^{3}-2x & 10x-5{x}^{3} \\ ({x}^{3}-2x)^{′} & (10x-5{x}^{3})^{′}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}{x}^{3}-2x & 10x-5{x}^{3} \\ 3{x}^{2}-2 & 10-15{x}^{2}\end{aligned}| \\  & =({x}^{3}-2x)(10-15{x}^{2})-(10x-5{x}^{3})(3{x}^{2}-2) \\  & =x({x}^{2}-2)\cdot 5(2-3{x}^{2})-5x(2-{x}^{2})(3{x}^{2}-2) \\  & =5x({x}^{2}-2)(2-3{x}^{2})-5x({x}^{2}-2)(2-3{x}^{2}) \\  & =-15{x}^{5}+40{x}^{3}-20x-(-15{x}^{5}+40{x}^{3}-20x) \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$

which is $\text{zero for all }x\in R.$

Therefore, the set ${{y}_{1}(x),{y}_{2}(x)}$ is linearly $\text{dependent}$ on $R.$

EXPLANATION

Suppose the functions y1(x) and y2(x) are defined on some interval I. The Wronskian W(y1,y2) of these functions is defined as W(y1,y2)=|y1y2y1′y2′|=y1y2′−y2y1′.

Recall the following:

  • If W≠0 for at least one x∈I, then y1 and y2 are linearly independent.

  • If W=0 and it’s known that y1 and y2 are solutions to the same second-order linear differential equation, then y1 and y2 are linearly dependent.

In our case, the Wronskian is given by

W(y1,y2)=|x3−2x10x−5x3(x3−2x)′(10x−5x3)′|=|x3−2x10x−5x33x2−210−15x2|=(x3−2x)(10−15x2)−(10x−5x3)(3x2−2)=x(x2−2)⋅5(2−3x2)−5x(2−x2)(3x2−2)=5x(x2−2)(2−3x2)−5x(x2−2)(2−3x2)=−15x5+40x3−20x−(−15x5+40x3−20x)=0

which is zero for all x∈R.

Therefore, the set {y1(x),y2(x)} is linearly dependent on R.
